items.reply: This is by design: the spec puts --shout before the name, and other argument orders are out of scope. `greet.sh ada --shout` prints `hello ada`, the same as before the change.

finding.proof: bin/greet.sh:9 runs `echo "${line}"` on a name taken from argv; under dash or macOS /bin/sh, `sh bin/greet.sh 'a\tb'` prints a real tab where the old printf printed a backslash and a t.
finding.claim: `echo` expands backslash sequences in the name on some POSIX sh builds, so names holding a backslash print differently from before the change.

items.note: True: `tr a-z A-Z` uppercases ASCII only, and its ranges are unspecified outside the C locale. The author limits names to ASCII and the spec asks for no more; `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'` is the portable form if that changes.

items.reply: The flag has to be kept in a variable: line 5 shifts `--shout` off so that `${1:-world}` reads the name, so by line 8 the argument is gone and a plain `if` on it can't work. `shout=yes|no` is the usual POSIX sh form, since sh has no booleans.

finding.claim: The tests cover only the plain greeting; nothing checks --shout, alone or with a name, though the spec's done-when asks for `--shout ada` to print HELLO ADA.
finding.suggestion: Add to tests/greet_test.sh: `[ "$(sh .../bin/greet.sh --shout)" = "HELLO WORLD" ]` and `[ "$(sh .../bin/greet.sh --shout ada)" = "HELLO ADA" ]`, using the same dirname path as line 3.

noticed.text: The MR's only commit message is `Add --shout`, with no typo; the resolved typo thread matches nothing in the commit as it is now.
The bot's item 2 cites line 8 for the `echo`; in the reviewed commit it is line 9 (line 8 is the `tr`).
